name: Blaxel
oneLiner: MicroVM sandboxes billed by allocated RAM, now part of Baseten.
whatItIs: Blaxel runs sandboxes as microVMs for agent workloads, alongside agent hosting, MCP servers, batch jobs and a model gateway.
Baseten acquired Blaxel on 10 September 2026. The announcement says the product continues and features keep shipping, and Baseten sign-in now connects to a Blaxel workspace.
whoFor: Teams building agent platforms that want instant sandboxes, a built-in MCP surface and optional agent hosting.
isolation: MicroVM boundary per sandbox, root by default with an optional unprivileged user. The default kernel refuses module loading and kernel tracing to every process, including root; iptables requires enabling at creation.
sizes: Memory drives CPU: 8 GB gets 4 cores and 16 GB gets 6. Custom deployments advertise up to 256 GB of RAM. Regions: Oregon, North Virginia, London and Frankfurt.

billing.model: Pay-as-you-go against a wallet, with quota tiers set by top-up.
billing.meter: $0.0000115 per GB of allocated RAM per second while active; CPU is included in that rate. Snapshot storage $0.20 per GB-month and volumes $0.12 per GB-month.
billing.stopped: Standby stops memory charges but keeps billing snapshot and volume storage.
billing.planFee: No subscription: tiers are wallet top-ups ($0, $20, $50) that raise quotas.
billing.minimum: No published minimum billed duration. Up to $200 in promotional credits is advertised; the actual grant is not published.

A.shape: 2 vCPU / 4 GiB, deleted after each task
notes: Assumes immediate deletion, so no snapshot or volume storage.
The 4 GB / 2 vCPU mapping is from a secondary source; CPU scales with memory.
A 50 GB volume is assumed because the local writable filesystem uses RAM.
Images and retained snapshots are extra.

C.headline: $17.30 plus snapshot storage
C.shape: 4 vCPU / 8 GiB, 20 GB volume, 90 active hours, 630 standby
notes: Standby snapshot storage adds S × $0.20 × 630/730, where S is billable GB and is not published.
Retaining a sandbox for the month needs a tier above free, which enforces a TTL.

facts.label: Legal entity

source.quote: Blaxel, Inc (formerly known as Beamlit, Inc.), a Delaware corporation, d/b/a Blaxel

facts.label: Ownership
facts.value: Acquired by Baseten on 10 September 2026. The linked terms predate the deal and still name Blaxel.

facts.label: Founded and funded
facts.value: 2024, by six founders including CEO Paul Sinaï. A $7.3M seed led by First Round.

source.quote: Blaxel raised a $7.3M seed round led by First Round.

facts.label: Headcount
facts.value: 12, per Y Combinator's directory. The figure is undated and not a post-acquisition count.

facts.label: Status and SLA
facts.value: Sandboxes 99.33% over July–October 2026. Custom SLAs only; no standard uptime commitment published.

facts.label: Certification
facts.value: SOC 2, HIPAA and ISO 27001 claimed; the full SOC 2 report is on request through its compliance portal.

well: A sandbox that must resume in milliseconds: standby preserves process state and resume is claimed under 25 ms.
Secrets that should never sit in the machine: the proxy injects headers, body fields and secrets server-side.
A team that wants SDKs in three languages, a console and a per-sandbox MCP server.
badly: A buyer who needs the contracting entity settled now: the terms still name Blaxel, not Baseten.
A workload that needs kernel modules or iptables without opting in at creation.
Production dependence on snapshots, which are in private preview.

usability.dashboard: A console creates a sandbox by choosing an image, resources, TTL and region, with a browser terminal.
usability.withoutCode: The console can create and inspect a sandbox, but useful work still needs commands or a developer.
usability.signup: Baseten or Blaxel sign-in. Card requirement and credit expiry are not published.
usability.docs: Documentation covers sandboxes, snapshots, volumes, MCP and SSO. A status page is linked from the site. Support is Discord community plus paid tiers.
tripsUp: Standby keeps memory but drops external connections.
Free and low tiers enforce expiration dates on sandboxes.
A volume attaches to one sandbox at a time; Agent Drive is the shared option.

caveats.issue: Idle timing is stated two ways
caveats.detail: The docs say a sandbox goes to standby after 15 minutes of idle WebSocket/TCP activity; the pricing FAQ says it scales to zero after about 5 seconds.

evidence.quote: if the WebSocket/TCP connection remains idle for 15 minutes with no activity, the sandbox will automatically transition to standby mode.
Sandboxes scale to zero after about 5 seconds of inactivity and resume from standby in roughly 25ms

caveats.issue: Snapshots and archive are private previews
caveats.detail: The snapshot docs say the feature is in private preview and not recommended for production; archive is also preview.
Baseten acquired Blaxel on 10 September 2026. The product continues, but a permanent standalone guarantee is not published.

caveats.issue: Low tiers delete sandboxes on a timer
caveats.detail: Tier 0 and Tier 1 enforce expiration dates of up to 7 and 30 days; activity is counted at resume or suspend, not in between.
A volume attaches to one sandbox at a time; Agent Drive is the multi-mount shared filesystem, and the two are separate products.

strengths: Standby preserves memory and processes, with a sub-25 ms resume claim.
Every sandbox exposes an MCP server for files, processes, ports and previews.
A secret proxy injects credentials into outbound HTTPS requests.
Agent Drive offers a shared filesystem across sandboxes.
Snapshots can outlive the sandbox and be forked.
